title: OpenClaw on Hostinger: managed or VPS? What each one requires and who it suits
seoTitle: OpenClaw on Hostinger: managed or VPS? How to choose
description: OpenClaw on Hostinger: managed is cheaper in the first period, and the VPS gives you root and Docker, plus who each one suits.

contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: Choose managed if you want the assistant running without looking after a server, and the VPS if you want root access and to run other programs on the same machine. Both options accept Hostinger's AI credits or your own API key. What matters is how much maintenance you are willing to take on.

contentSections.heading: What OpenClaw is
paragraphs: OpenClaw is an open-source AI assistant under the MIT license. It runs on a computer or server, keeps conversations, memory and credentials on that machine, and answers through the messaging apps you already use, such as Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack and Discord. To think and reply, it uses AI models from other companies, such as Claude, GPT and Gemini, which charge for usage.

The project itself costs nothing: the official README says it has no paid plan, no hosted service and no token. What costs money is the server it runs on and the use of the AI models. At Hostinger, there are two paths:
bullets: **Managed:** you buy the plan, and Hostinger installs, updates and maintains the assistant.

**VPS:** you rent a virtual server, and Hostinger installs OpenClaw on it with Docker, a program that runs each application isolated in a container. From then on, updates and server security are yours.

contentSections.heading: Managed or VPS: the table
paragraphs: Managed is the "AI automation apps" plan, the same one used for Hermes Agent and Paperclip, at the same price, and it is cheaper than the VPS in the first period.

postParagraphs: An API key is the password OpenClaw uses to ask an AI provider for answers. The provider charges for that use, directly to you.

contentSections.heading: What the plan does not cover
postParagraphs: The plan is not the whole cost: AI usage is charged separately. With Hostinger's credits, the managed plan comes with a starting balance, and whatever goes beyond it is charged by use. The price of a top-up does not appear on any public page, so check the panel before you count on it. With your own key, the provider (OpenAI, Anthropic or another) charges you directly, depending on the model and the number of conversations.

The managed plan has a 30-day refund window. On the VPS, the 30 days apply only if your last VPS refund was requested more than 180 days ago. A VPS of 12 months or more comes with a free .cloud or .tech domain for the first year.

contentSections.heading: Telegram and WhatsApp
paragraphs: Both channels work on both options. The difference is where you set them up. On managed, you pick the channels in Hostinger's setup assistant: for WhatsApp, you scan a QR code; for Telegram, you paste the bot token. On the VPS, the setup has optional fields for the WhatsApp number, with country code, and for the Telegram bot token. The documentation does not show where the WhatsApp QR appears on the VPS.
For Telegram, there are three steps:

image.alt: Three steps to connect OpenClaw to Telegram: create the bot in BotFather and copy the token, paste the token into OpenClaw's configuration, and send a message to approve the first contact
image.caption: The steps from OpenClaw's official documentation.

bullets: Create the bot in BotFather, Telegram's official bot for creating bots, and copy the token.
Paste the token into OpenClaw's configuration.
Send a message to the bot. Anyone not yet approved receives a pairing code, and you approve the first contact in the OpenClaw panel.
postParagraphs: On WhatsApp, OpenClaw joins as a linked device, like WhatsApp Web, and login is by QR code only. The documentation recommends using a number separate from your personal one.

contentSections.heading: Security: when the decision changes
paragraphs: The question is who looks after the data and the credentials. On managed, Hostinger says each instance runs isolated in a container, with its own security gateway. That is Hostinger's description, not a test of ours. On the VPS, Hostinger itself says that, with root access, the setup, the updates and the security are the responsibility of whoever bought it.

OpenClaw's security policy says it is built for one trusted person, not for several people who do not know each other: whoever can talk to the assistant can make it use its tools. That changes the choice in three cases:
bullets: **More than one person will use the assistant** (family or team): the project recommends one server per person. On the VPS, that is straightforward; on managed, ask Hostinger how many instances one account can have.

**The assistant will have access to your email, your bank or other accounts:** the project asks that the server have no personal accounts logged in. Hostinger suggests a separate mailbox for the assistant.
**On the VPS, keep the gateway token** that the installation generates, and don't send it in a conversation with the assistant.

contentSections.heading: Who should choose which
bullets: you want the assistant online without installing or configuring a server;
you prefer Hostinger to take care of updates, backups and security;
you don't know what root or Docker is;
you want OpenClaw, or to switch to Hermes Agent or Paperclip on the same plan.
postParagraphs: **Choose the VPS if:** you want root access and to run other programs on the same server, such as a website or n8n; you know your way around a server, or want to learn, and accept updating and securing the system; or you need more memory and disk: KVM plans range from 4 GB to 32 GB of RAM.
**If in doubt, start with managed.** It costs less in the first period and doesn't require server knowledge.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: Is Hostinger's managed OpenClaw worth it? It is for people who want the assistant without looking after a server: it costs less than the VPS in the first period and renews at the same price. Anyone who wants root access and other programs on the server is better off with the VPS.
Do you need an OpenAI or Anthropic account? No. On both options you can use Hostinger's AI credits. You only need an account with a provider if you prefer your own key.
Is there a Hostinger discount coupon for OpenClaw? Yes: the code SONAR20, in the cart's coupon field, gives 20% off the first period.

Does the managed plan work for Hermes Agent or Paperclip? Yes. All three are on the same plan, "AI automation apps", at the same price. The Paperclip page does not list AI credits, so bring your own key.
